title: Model availability sentinel & probabilistic cost scan
creator: Arielle Kim
description: Problem: We need an automated, product-facing signal layer that detects model availability disruptions (downtimes, quota throttles, region outages, sudden deprecations) and estimates the live economic impact of forced fallbacks. Current scouting and procurement both react too slowly: customers experience latency spikes or cost blowouts when the primary model becomes unavailable and teams scramble to switch variants.
objectives: Design a lightweight sentinel manifest that tracks model liveness, regional capacity health, and pricing elasticity across our curated model catalog.

Produce a probabilistic cost scan that simulates fallback paths (hosted -> dedicated -> private variants) under realistic traffic mixes to estimate expected token-cost and latency delta over a 72h window.
Ship an initial dashboard + alerting rules for SRE/Procurement to trigger capacity buys / canary rollouts when forecasted fallback risk > threshold.
scope_notes: Scope covers signal ingestion (heartbeat scraping, provider status feeds, quota telemetry), a lightweight forecasting engine (time-series + bootstrapped scenario sampler), and an initial UI surface in Console. Excludes automated procurement approvals (handled by a follow-up PM).
design_decisions: Use conservative sensitivity to avoid frequent false positives: threshold defaults to 10% predicted availability loss over 24h.
Prefer synthesized workload replay (customer archetypes) over raw historical cost averages to capture latency/cost interactions at token-distribution tails.
Expose both probabilistic and worst-case mode in dashboard; alerts default to probabilistic to prevent alert fatigue.
tradeoffs: Higher sensitivity detects problems earlier but increases false positives and operational churn.
Running frequent synthetic replays increases infra cost; we'll start with a nightly low-cost sampler and request on-demand full replays for high-risk signals.
Integrating provider-side signals (official status pages) is fast but incomplete; we will combine with active probes and telemetry buckets for coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel ingest pipeline captures >= 90% of critical model variants across 3 major regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-south).
Probabilistic scan produces a 72h cost+latency delta estimate within ±20% of full replay for pilot workloads.
Dashboard shows top-5 at-risk models and can generate a PDF summary report for procurement.
updates: 2026-03-11 - Kickoff sync with ENG runtime team: agreed on telemetry tags (model_id, region, variant, commit_hash) and a light-weight probe endpoint; ENG to provide schema by 2026-03-17.
2026-03-12 - PM research: interviewed three enterprise customers; common ask is advance notice of fallback window > 2 hours and estimated token-cost delta.
2026-03-13 - Design feedback: Console team recommends embedding a scenario selector (conservative, typical, aggressive) instead of exposing raw sampler params to users.
2026-03-14 - Legal/Procurement consult: procurement favors advisory alerts for the first phase (no auto-commit). Follow-up to scope procurement automation in Q2.
2026-03-15 - Decision: implement nightly low-cost sampling + on-demand full-scan; pilot in us-east and eu-west for two weeks.
